Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase! The umpires are back out in the middle and the players of India Women have taken their places on the field. It will be the pair of Qiana Joseph and Hayley Matthews to open the innings for West Indies Women. Renuka Singh Thakur has the new ball in hand and is raring to go. Let's play...
... The Run Chase ...

As West Indies Women prepare to embark on their run chase, the question lingers in the air - Can they successfully chase down the target, or will the India Women's bowling unit rise to the challenge? The stage is set for a riveting second innings, where every run and wicket will shape the narrative of this encounter. Stay tuned as the drama unfolds in the pursuit of victory between the West Indies Women and India Women.

West Indies Women's plan to win the game started working since the toss. Chinelle Henry drew the first blood for the Windies and within a couple of overs they cleaned the whole top order of the Women in Blues. Things took a slight turn as after they got the third wicket, they failed to pick more successive wickets which allowed the opposition to keep the scoreboard ticking to build confidence and the partnership strong at the same time. Nonetheless, the skipper once again stepped up to break the partnership before it got out of their hands. At the end of the inning, Hayley Matthews picked up four into her account and Chinelle Henry as well as Ashmini Munisar chipped in for a wicket each.

Jemimah Rodrigues and Yastika Bhatia shook their hands to anchor the inning from 23 for 3 in the 6th over to 73 in the 14th over. Bhatia got a lifeline as well in the 10th over but failed to cash out big figures from it. But Rodrigues once again kept her composure on the track and went on with her lusty blows to gain her 12th half-century in this T20I format. But as soon as she crossed her 50 mark, a miscommunication resulted in a run-out, where she had to lose her wicket. The lower middle over of the team did enough to put a target of 142 runs on the board, and surely the skipper, Harmanpreet Kaur would be much happier as things went slightly better from the worse.

What a magnificent inning from the 24-year-old Jemimah Rodrigues to pull up the strings for the Women in Blues. India Women had a nervy start to begin their inning but in the end, things turned out to be something better than the team thought after the first six overs. Shafali Verma and Smriti Mandhana opened their pair for the Blues but lost their first partnership pretty early.

On the other side, the Windies will be led by Hayley Matthews. The last time the side played against the Blues was back in February of 2020 when they lost the encounter just by 2 runs. They have a good number of all-rounders and middle-order batters to bring more stability in the mid-inning. Hayley Matthews will be the spearhead of the batting as well as bowling order. Deandra Dottin also holds a pretty impressive average in the batting unit. Karishma Ramharack will be a crucial player as the stadiums of UAE are a bit inclined towards the spinners. Stay tuned for toss updates and live action!

India Women last played against Bangladesh, in February 2023 in this format. The team looked pretty compact and the Indian fans would hope to see the same picture in this match. The top order looks solid, with Yastika Bhatia, Shafali Verma and the fan favorite Smriti Mandhana. The recent action of Mandhana in The Hundred was not up to the mark but if we are talking about the performance of The Hundred we need to draw attention to Deepti Sharma. Her immense performance played an important role in winning the championship and stole the headlines of articles. So cricketing fans all over the world will surely keep an eye on her. The middle order also has the perfect balance of young blood like Richa Ghosh and Jemimah Rodrigues, and the experience of the skipper Harmanpreet Kaur. Pooja Vastrakar as well gives more stability to the lower middle order with her lusty blows to turn the tides of the game. In the bowling unit, Renuka Singh Thakur would lead the pace attack with Vastrakar. In the spin department, Shreyanka Patil and Radha Yadav are always there to increase the depth to offer some spin on the track.

Hello and a warm welcome to all our viewers tuning in for the buildup! The stage is set for the clash of the India Women and West Indies Women in Dubai. Yes, it's a warm-up match but the intent to get the win would be thriving as both sides would be looking to build their momentum for the T20 World Cup.
... MATCHDAY ...

The biggest stage in women’s cricket is set to unfold, and the world is buzzing in anticipation for the ICC Women's T20 World Cup 2024 in the UAE. Excitement is palpable as 10 teams, divided into two groups, battle it out for the top two spots in their respective groups to advance to the semifinals. Australia, the defending champions and a powerhouse in the women’s game, have lifted the trophy six times, making them the clear favourites once again. However, India, England, and West Indies are strong contenders, and the rest of the teams should not be underestimated, making for an incredibly exciting tournament. Each team will play two warm-up games, giving them valuable time to acclimate to the conditions and fine-tune their strategies and team combinations. All eyes now shift to warm-up match number 4, where India Women take on West Indies Women at the ICC Academy Ground No. 2 in Dubai. West Indies Women, led by Hayley Matthews, have a balanced squad with a solid mix of experience and youth. Deandra Dottin’s return from retirement is a huge boost for them along with her all-round prowess. Stafanie Taylor will also be a key player for the women in red. Although the bowling unit lacks some experience, the overall talent topped with the depth in their all-rounders make West Indies a formidable side. On the other hand, India Women have been consistent performers in ICC tournaments but have struggled to handle the pressure of knockout stages. They are certainly serious contenders for the trophy, led by the dynamic Harmanpreet Kaur. India's recent form has been stellar, and the team has settled into a well-balanced unit. Their batting is a significant strength, with power hitters like Shafali Verma and Smriti Mandhana at the top, followed by the reliable middle order with the likes of Harmanpreet Kaur and Jemimah Rodrigues. What truly sets India Women apart is their potent spin attack, which is expected to be a major weapon in the spin-friendly conditions of the UAE. Both teams will be looking to use this warm-up game to get into rhythm and adjust to the conditions before the main event kicks off. With two powerhouse teams clashing in what promises to be a tightly contested match, this game will serve as a perfect tune-up for the battles to come.
